full_judgment: 9. It is stated that all the awardees were Muslim and no one was of the Hindu faith. Therefore, the claim of owning the 1.10 acres of the acquired land under khatian No. 1687 appertaining to plot No. 41 of Mouza Sylhet Municipality JL No. 91 by Mr Rajani Ranjan Gupta and his son Rukshimini Ranjan Gupta is not true. It is stated that no such person/persons in the name of Rajani Ranjan Gupta and Rukshuini Ranjan Gupta were present at the time of acquisition of the said land as they had left the defunct East Pakistan during the Hindu-Muslim Riot on transfer of their land property to the awardees of the LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, but the settlement Amla of the EBSA & T Act, 1950 AD had recorded 1.10 acres of land under Khatian No. 1687 appertaining to plot No. 41 in the name of Rajani Ranjan Gupta in their absence, which enticed the land grabbers of the Sylhet town to make one fake Rukshini Ranjan Gupta son of late Rajani Ranjan Gupta and successfully transferred lands in favour of (1) Mr Abdus Shahed, 0.25 acres, (2) Mr Abdul Moyed, 0.25 acres, (3) Md Sirajul Islam, 0.20 acres, (4) Mosammat Kulsuma Begum, 0.25 acres, (5) Mr Ashish Chowdhury, 0.20 acres, in total 1.10 acres. It is stated that the whole area of the acquired land under the LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 was abated by the Tahsilder, Sylhet Municipality Tahsil vide his memo No. 87 dated 27-4-1968. It is stated that it is evident from the register of land acquisition (LA) section that at the request of the director of fisheries E-P, Dhaka vide his letter dated 31-4-64, the possession of an area of 5.59 acres of land covered by Plots. No. 33, 34, 40, 41 and 42 in full, and Plots No. 43 and 44 in parts at Mouza Sylhet Municipality JL No. 91 was handed over to the District Fishery Officer, Sylhet on 28-5-1964 upon requisitioning the same for setting up a Whole Sale Fish Market at Sylhet.
